prs.author: MukundaKatta
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCP exception classes (UrlElicitationRequiredError and MCPError subclasses) are not pickle-safe because their __init__ signatures diverge from the default pickle reconstruction path. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCP exception classes (UrlElicitationRequiredError and MCPError subclasses) are not pickle-safe because their __init__ signatures diverge from the default pickle reconstruction path. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2478 addresses the broader class of the problem: it adds a module-level _restore_mcp_error dispatcher that handles any MCPError subclass (routing UrlElicitationRequiredError through from_error and all others through from_error_data), which is the correct pattern for subclass-safe pickling. PR #2439 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, leaving all other MCPError subclasses still broken. PR #2478 also removes an incorrect pragma: no cover on the data property as a clean-up. The trade-off is that PR #2478's dispatch function is slightly more indirection, but it's the only approach that doesn't require each future subclass to re-implement __reduce__ independently.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs add an identical `capability_filter` parameter to `MCPServer.__init__` and store it as `self._capability_filter`, starting from the same base commit (59de0ace4). They solve the exact same problem: filtering advertised server capabilities to only those backed by registered primitives. (2 PRs)
